title: Zariski local fs monoid charts for a Zariski log structure
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Suppose there is a log structure $M_{\mathrm{Zar}}\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ on the Zariski site whose associated etale log structure is $M$; here a log structure has the same monoid-sheaf and inverse-image-of-units axiom as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], on the indicated site. For every point $x\in X$ there are an affine Zariski open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a fine saturated commutative monoid $P$, and a homomorphism $h:P\to M_{\mathrm{Zar}}(U)$ such that the log structure associated on the Zariski site to $\alpha h:P\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is $M_{\mathrm{Zar}}|_U$, and its associated etale log structure is $M|_U$. Thus $h$ is a chart on both sites, with the prescribed structural map.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107, last sentence (Zariski fine log schemes have Zariski local fine monoscheme charts); fs refinement by taking the sharp characteristic monoid, as in VI 1.6 and VIII 3.3.13, printed pp.70,108--109.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, a geometric point $\bar x$ over it, and an fs etale chart $Q$ near $\bar x$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $L=(M_{\mathrm{Zar}})_x$. The Zariski-stalk unit-extension lemma says that $L$ is integral, has units $A^\times$, and identifies its sharpening $P=L/A^\times$ with $(Q-E)/E^{\mathrm{gp}}$, where $E$ is the face mapping to units in $B$. Face sharpening therefore makes $P$ sharp fine saturated and $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ finite free. Apply the integral-monoid splitting lemma to $L$: it gives $j:P\to L$ and an isomorphism $P\oplus A^\times\to L$, $(p,u)\mapsto j(p)u$. No nonzero $p\in P$ has $\alpha j(p)\in B^\times$: the local map $A\to B$ reflects units, so $\alpha j(p)\in A^\times$, hence $j(p)\in\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)=A^\times$ by the unit axiom of $M_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, and $p=q(j(p))=0$, where $q:L\to P$ is the quotient map with $qj=\mathrm{id}$ from the splitting lemma. So the face $(\alpha j)^{-1}(A^\times)$, and likewise its preimage of $B^\times$, is $\{0\}$, and the chart pushouts over it are the products $P\oplus A^\times$ and $P\oplus B^\times$. The unit-extension formula $L\oplus_{A^\times}B^\times\simeq M_{\bar x}$ with $L\simeq P\oplus A^\times$ then identifies $P\oplus B^\times\to M_{\bar x}$, $(p,b)\mapsto j(p)b$, with an isomorphism too. Thus the composite $j_{\mathrm{Et}}:P\to M_{\bar x}$ is a chart of that stalk, and $j$ is a chart of the Zariski stalk.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators $p_1,\ldots,p_d$ of $P$. The finite-presentation lemma supplies finitely many defining pairs of relations for these generators. Represent each germ $j(p_i)$ by a section of $M_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ on a common Zariski neighborhood $U_0$ of $x$. Each relation holds at $x$, so its two section representatives agree on a smaller neighborhood. Intersect these finitely many neighborhoods. The resulting tuple satisfies every defining relation and hence determines a homomorphism $h:P\to M_{\mathrm{Zar}}(U_0)$ with germ exactly $j$. This uses only the definition of equality of germs after the cited finite-presentation result; empty generator or relation lists require no shrinking.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: On $U_0$ put $\beta=\alpha h$. Apply the Zariski prelog-logification comparison to the constant monoid sheaf associated to $P$ and to $\beta$. Denote its associated Zariski log structure by $N_Z$ and its associated etale log structure by $N$. The universal properties give compatible maps $f_Z:N_Z\to M_{\mathrm{Zar}}|_{U_0}$ and $f:N\to M|_{U_0}$, induced by $h$ and fixing units. The comparison identifies the etale extension of $f_Z$ with $f$. The etale associated-log stalk formula identifies $f_{\bar x}$ with the isomorphism $P\oplus B^\times\to M_{\bar x}$ in step 1, respecting the specified generators and structural map.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: Apply fine-log stalk-chart spreading to the given map $j_{\mathrm{Et}}:P\to M_{\bar x}$. Its pushout hypothesis was verified in step 1. It gives an affine pointed etale neighborhood $(W,\bar w)\to(U_0,\bar x)$ and a chart $k:P\to M(W)$ whose germ is $j_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The homomorphism obtained from $h$ on $W$ has the same germ. The equality clause of finite-monoid stalk-data spreading gives a further affine pointed etale refinement on which these homomorphisms agree. Replace $W$ by this refinement; restrictions of a chart are charts by associated-log restriction compatibility. Thus the restriction of $f$ to $W$ is an isomorphism induced by exactly $h$, not by an unrelated chart with the same abstract monoid.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: Let $V$ be the image of this $W\to U_0$. It contains $x$ and is Zariski open by openness of etale morphisms. The map $W\to V$ is a surjective etale covering. For any geometric point $\bar y$ of $V$, the geometric-point lifting lemma gives a lift to $W$. The restriction-stalk identification in finite-monoid stalk-data spreading identifies the map $f_{\bar y}$ with the stalk of $f|_W$, which is an isomorphism by step 4. The geometric-stalk criterion for etale sheaves now makes $f|_V$ an isomorphism. In particular $N|_V$ is fs, using the charts of the isomorphic $M|_V$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), p.107, agent descent argument; Stacks 03WT (morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-open), 03PR and 03PU (etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover and theorem-exactness-stalks).

proof.text: Fix $y\in V$ and a geometric point $\bar y$ over it. Write $C=\mathcal O_{V,y}$, $D=\mathcal O_{V,\bar y}$, $R_1=(N_Z)_y$, $R_2=(M_{\mathrm{Zar}})_y$ and $a=(f_Z)_y$. Apply Zariski-stalk unit extension to both Zariski log structures, whose associated etale log structures are fs by step 5. It says that $R_i$ are integral with units $C^\times$, and canonically identifies their characteristic quotients with those of $R_i\oplus_{C^\times}D^\times$. These identifications respect section maps and units. Since $f_{\bar y}$ is an isomorphism, the induced map $\overline a:R_1/C^\times\to R_2/C^\times$ is bijective. Thus we have a bijection on characteristic monoids for the actual Zariski map, not merely an abstract identification of them.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: The map $a$ in step 6 is bijective by cancellation. For $b\in R_2$, lift its characteristic using $\overline a$ to a representative $r\in R_1$. Then $b=a(r)u$ for some $u\in C^\times$, so $b=a(ru)$. If $a(r)=a(s)$, injectivity of $\overline a$ gives $r=su$ for a unit $u\in C^\times$. Cancellation in the integral monoid $R_2$ yields $u=1$, since $a$ fixes units; hence $r=s$. Therefore all Zariski stalk maps of $f_Z|_V$ are bijective. On any open, a target section has local lifts by stalk surjectivity; injectivity of stalks makes any two local lifts equal after shrinking at each point of an overlap. The sheaf uniqueness and gluing axioms give a unique global lift. Thus $f_Z|_V$ is an isomorphism compatible with the structural maps.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighborhood $T$ of $x$ in $X$. In $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, basic opens form a basis: since $x\in V\cap T$, the complement is a closed set $V(I)$, and some $g\in I$ is outside the prime of $x$. Then $U=D_T(g)=\operatorname{Spec}R_g$ contains $x$ and is contained in $V$. Restrict $h$ to $U$. Restriction compatibility for logification preserves the isomorphisms $N_Z|_U\simeq M_{\mathrm{Zar}}|_U$ and $N|_U\simeq M|_U$ from steps 5 and 7. Consequently $P$ is the required fs chart on both sites and its structural map is exactly $\alpha h$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii), printed p.107; VI 3.7(a), printed p.75; agent expansion of the Zariski chart construction.
